name: Taipei Fine Arts Museum
funding: Taipei City agency; 2025-26 sponsors incl. CTBC Culture & Education Fdn (bank), Chanel, Friends of TFAM, Winsing Arts Fdn, Luce Fdn.
watch: Artist-run association of 60+ members. Dec 2021: Venice pavilion paused over Sakuliu assault claims; victim's lawyer said TFAM's name was used to pressure her.
records_note: Annual reports 2006 to 2024, yearly budget and final accounts 2014 to 2025 and a dated sponsor directory are on its site; no board.

name: Palais de Lomé
funding: Togolese state paid the XOF 2.2bn renovation and funds operations. Director Sonia Lawson sought sponsors in 2019. CFAO and Toyota Tsusho hosted an award show in June 2026.
watch: No censorship, cancelled show or protest found.
records_note: No reports, accounts or board are published; the patrons thank-you page says its content will be available soon.

name: Ishara Art Foundation
funding: Self-funded by founder Smita Prabhakar, who directs AMS International, a Dubai HR and events firm. Based at Alserkal Avenue; Abdelmonem Alserkal is honorary chairman of the trustees.
watch: The National (2024): 'completely self-funded'. A 2017 profile also lists her at Lazer Capital (infrastructure, oil and gas); no source links it to Ishara.
records_note: The site lists its trustees and advisory board; it publishes no annual reports, accounts or funders.

name: Hospitalfield
funding: £839k income (FY2025); Creative Scotland, Historic Environment Scotland, National Lottery Heritage Fund, Foyle Foundation, Robertson Trust, Garfield Weston Foundation, William Grant Foundation.
records_note: No annual reports; OSCR holds accounts for 2020 to 2025, the Future Plan page names funders without a date, and the board is listed.

name: Holburne Museum
funding: Public funders are the National Lottery Heritage Fund and Community Fund. Trusts include Garfield Weston, AKO, Clore Duffield and the Blavatnik Family Foundation; Bloomberg Philanthropies backed the website.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies listed for digital support.
records_note: Posts trustees' reports and signed accounts for 2016 to 2024, names its eleven directors and keeps a named supporters list with no date.

name: Belfast Exposed
funding: Arts Council of Northern Ireland and Belfast City Council, per its support page. A 2024 interview adds trusts and foundations, unnamed.
watch: Both bodies are on the Arts Council NI 2025/26 funding lists. No controversy, protest or censorship found.
records_note: The NI charity register holds its annual reports 2023 to 2024 and accounts to 2025; funders show as logos and no board is listed.

name: Golden Thread Gallery
funding: £400k income (FY2025); Arts Council NI, National Lottery, Belfast City Council, Art Fund, Gulbenkian, Ireland Funds, Ampersand, Future Screens NI.
watch: The Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation, a current funder, is endowed by an oil fortune and held oil firm Partex until 2019; protesters objected in 2016.
why_flagged: £400k income (FY2025); Arts Council NI, National Lottery, Belfast City Council, Art Fund, Gulbenkian, Ireland Funds, Ampersand, Future Screens NI.
records_note: Shows funder logos with no names or date, and posts no annual reports, accounts or board; the company is on the Northern Ireland register.

name: Wysing Arts Centre
funding: £863k income (FY2025); ACE NPO, Freelands Fdn (Murdoch media money), Garfield Weston, Ragdoll, Art Fund, local councils, Thalia Waste.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Site names no funders beyond patrons. Thalia Waste Management (landfill fund) and the John Armitage Charitable Trust (hedge-fund money) are allowed, named here.
records_note: No annual reports; accounts 2021 to 2025 are on the Charity Commission register; the support page names funders, undated; a board of trustees is listed.

name: Firstsite
funding: £2.4M income (FY2025); core funders ACE, Colchester and Essex councils; Garfield Weston, Essex Community Fdn, Attwells Solicitors.
watch: UNVERIFIED: Site blocked; other funders not verifiable. Name to know: Bloomberg Philanthropies Digital Accelerator (Jan 2025). Also a 2018 conflict-of-interest case and a 2026 complaint about nudity in the Duncan Grant show.
records_note: No annual reports; accounts are on the Charity Commission register; a thank-you page names funders, undated; only senior staff are listed, no board.

name: Grizedale Arts
funding: £469k income; Arts Council England and South Lakeland council per site; recent grants: Royal Countryside Fund 2025, Lottery Community Fund, Foyle.
records_note: No annual reports; accounts 2021 to 2025 are on the Charity Commission register; the home page names two funders, undated; trustees are listed.

name: Void
funding: Arts Council NI, Derry City and Strabane District Council, Future Screens NI, Garfield Weston Foundation, Halifax Foundation NI, Henry Moore Foundation, Ulster University; early build funded by Peace II.
records_note: The NI register holds annual reports 2023 to 2024 and accounts to 2025; the about page names funders undated and lists eight board members.

name: Talbot Rice Gallery
funding: University of Edinburgh gallery; 2025-26 shows credit ECA, Creative Scotland, Henry Moore Fdn, British Council, MGS, Polish culture ministry.
watch: Wael Shawky show (2025) co-funded by the Alwaleed Centre, endowed by Saudi Prince Alwaleed bin Talal.
records_note: The gallery publishes nothing itself; the University of Edinburgh posts annual reports, accounts and its Court; the gallery names funders only on exhibition pages.
